source.author: ov
source.text: Quae postquam Tethys, fatorum ignara nepotis reppulit, et facta est immensi copia caeli, corripuere viam pedibusque per aera motis obstantes scindunt nebulas pennisque levati praetereunt ortos isdem de partibus Euros.
source.text_original: Quae postquam Tethys, fatorum ignara nepotis / reppulit, et facta est immensi copia caeli, / corripuere viam pedibusque per aera motis / obstantes scindunt nebulas pennisque levati / praetereunt ortos isdem de partibus Euros.
source.text_english: When Tethys, unaware of her grandson’s fate, had pushed them back, and the whole vast sky was open to them, they seized the path; and, setting their feet in motion through the air, they cleave the clouds that bar their way and, lifted on their wings, pass by the Eurus that had risen from the same quarter.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: it pariter propulsa ratis; stant litore matres claraque vela oculis percussaque sole secuntur scuta virum, donec iam celsior arbore pontus immensusque ratem spectantibus abstulit aer.
reuse.text_original: it pariter propulsa ratis; stant litore matres / claraque vela oculis percussaque sole secuntur / scuta virum, donec iam celsior arbore pontus / immensusque ratem spectantibus abstulit aer.
reuse.text_english: The ship, driven on together, goes; mothers stand on the shore and, with their eyes, follow the bright sails and the shields of the men, struck by the sun, until the sea, now higher than the trees, and the vast air carried the ship away from the viewers.
